extracted.intended_audience: community members, homeowners, businesses, emergency managers, scientists, government officials, and partner organizations interested in earthquake resilience in Cascadia and the western U.S.
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational 'About / Contact' page for the Cascadia Region Earthquake Workgroup (CREW) describing its mission, methods, activities, goals, geographic scope, and contact information for those interested in engagement or membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — holistic risk reduction with mitigation centerpiece
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of CREW is to promote holistic risk reduction approaches, with mitigation as the cornerstone, and to foster the partnerships needed for the creation of more sustainable, risk-resistant environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes mitigation as primary strategy and partnership-building as necessary to create sustainable, risk-resistant environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration across public and private sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: CREW recognizes that planning for earthquakes and achieving resilience requires collaboration and input from both public and private sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values and works closely with many agencies and organizations that identify, study, monitor, and predict earthquakes and related hazards; implies that effective planning must incorporate diverse stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and facilitate rather than duplicate technical agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: CREW functions as an organizer and facilitator, bringing together public, private, and non-profit organizations, including researchers, practitioners, business owners, and community members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes CREW’s role from technical agencies — CREW’s value is in convening, coordinating, and fostering relationships rather than performing the technical monitoring/research itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-jurisdictional, regional approach
rubrics_metrics.description: By developing and fostering relationships, projects, products, and events that span city, state, and national boundaries, CREW helps both individual communities and regions raise awareness, develop mitigation strategies, and build resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes solutions and activities that cross jurisdictional boundaries to address the regional nature of earthquake hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work should be coordinated, consistent with best practices, and cost effective
rubrics_metrics.description: CREW helps communities build resilience in ways that are coordinated, consistent with best practices, and cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets evaluative desiderata for projects and strategies: coordination, adherence to best practices, and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — publish timely and accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes timely and accurate information for the use of public and private sector decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information produced should be both timely and accurate and targeted at decision-makers in public and private sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — sponsor and facilitate discussions on emerging issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and facilitates discussions on emerging issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement includes convening discourse around new or evolving earthquake-related topics to inform stakeholders and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — host quarterly meetings and business round tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosts quarterly meetings and business round tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly scheduled convenings are a mechanism for stakeholder engagement and information exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — produce planning guides and other resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces planning guides and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates practical products (guides, resources) meant to assist planning and mitigation efforts at community or organizational levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — respond to media requests for information and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Responds to media requests for information and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an expert source for public-facing communications to ensure accurate public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity — maintain website as guide and gateway
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains this website as a guide and gateway to the many community, state, and federal resources devoted to earthquake hazards and how to plan for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The website should function as a curated portal linking to resources and guidance from multiple levels of government and organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — reduce loss of life and property damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote efforts to reduce the loss of life and property damage from earthquakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary outcome-oriented goal: activities and programs should contribute to reductions in fatalities and property damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — educate and motivate decision makers and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate and motivate decision makers, managers, and the general public to reduce risks associated with earthquakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes both education and motivation as levers for behavior and policy change across multiple audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal — foster linkages among scientists, infrastructure providers, businesses, and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster productive linkages between scientists, critical infrastructure providers, businesses, and governmental agencies in order to improve the resilience of communities after an earthquake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on building cross-sector networks that enable coordinated response and recovery, and improve community resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope — Cascadia and broader western U.S. engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: CREW formed to address hazards in the Pacific Northwest (Cascadia) and has expanded its mission to include engagement with partner organizations across the western U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the regional focus for activities and partnerships: primary emphasis on Cascadia with extension to western U.S. partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership and engagement invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome all individuals, businesses, and organizations that want to make Cascadia and the western region more resilient to earthquakes and related hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open invitation criteria: individuals, businesses, and organizations interested in resilience are encouraged to join or engage; contact provided (info@crew.org).
